item.title: Meta Sued Over Training Data for Its AI and Face-Recognition Systems
item.description: The proposed class action alleges Meta illegally harvested people’s Facebook and Instagram photos to train its AI image-generation models and to build its unreleased “NameTag” face recognition feature.

item.title: One of AI’s Fiercest Critics Says All the Doom Talk Is ‘Meant to Distract Us’
item.description: Timnit Gebru argues that AI companies are stoking fears of extinction to avoid discussing actual harms, like autonomous weapons.

item.title: Why So Many AI Researchers Think the Machines Could Kill Everyone
item.description: A combination of rapid advances, recursive self-improvement, and agentic swarms are genuinely “spooking people” inside big labs.

item.title: OpenAI Wants to Know if an AI Industry Slowdown Would Even Be Legal
item.description: AI leaders worry antitrust law could stand in the way of what they view as an increasingly urgent push to coordinate a slowdown in AI development.

item.title: Is AI Actually Going to Kill Us All?
item.description: This week on “Uncanny Valley,” we dig into a former Anthropic researcher’s AI doomsday warning, the latest upgrades from Apple’s event, and the census report that claimed Trump won the 2020 election.

item.title: Everything New You Can Do With Siri AI
item.description: When iOS 27 arrives, it will bring with it a fully revamped assistant for your iPhone.

item.title: Clearview AI Is Testing an AI Tool That Would Let Cops Unearth Your Life Online
item.description: InquiryIQ, a previously unreported prototype, tested a model from xAI, maker of Grok, to surface associates, social accounts, and other information about people identified through Clearview.

item.title: The AI Researcher Who Just Quit Anthropic Says It’s ‘Crunch Time for Humanity’
item.description: Jacob Coxon talks to WIRED about the “mini Manhattan project” inside Anthropic, the problem with alignment, and why AI labs have just a few years left to make their systems safe.

item.title: San Francisco Orders Meta to Stop ‘Allowing’ AI Child Abuse Ads
item.description: The City Attorney’s Office has asked Meta to explain how the harmful ads repeatedly ran on Facebook and Instagram. The company claims the ads are not under the city’s jurisdiction.

item.title: I Let an AI Agent Hack All My Gadgets—and I’d Do It Again
item.description: After I removed the safety guardrails from a powerful open-source model, it found vulnerabilities in my household devices and hacked into a PC. But it also told me how to make everything a lot more secure.
